title: Attacking with Purpose
description: Score goals with smart decisions and teamwork!

questions.question: What should you do if you're in a 2v1 situation?
options: Try to dribble the defender alone
Pass to your teammate if the defender comes to you
Shoot from far away
Pass backwards
questions.explanation: Draw the defender in, then pass to your open teammate.

questions.question: What is the goal of an attacking play?
options: To keep possession without moving forward
To get the ball wide every time
To score or create a chance to score
To dribble until a defender steps in
questions.explanation: Every attack should move toward scoring or threatening the goal.

questions.question: An overlap is when:
options: A teammate runs around the outside to get ahead of the ball
A teammate drops behind the ball to defend
Two attackers stand in the same passing lane
A defender steps into midfield
questions.explanation: Overlapping creates confusion for defenders and passing options.

questions.question: When is a good time to dribble instead of pass?
options: When you're alone and have space
When 3 defenders are in front
When a safer forward pass is open
Every time you receive wide
questions.explanation: Use dribbling when there's space or you can beat a single player.

questions.question: Why is it smart to keep your head up while attacking?
options: To scan defenders, teammates, and open space
To focus only on the sideline
To slow down every attack
To avoid passing through midfield
questions.explanation: Good attackers scan for options while moving.

questions.question: A through ball is:
options: A pass into open space behind the defenders
A shot from far away
A pass that always goes backward
A cross from the corner area
questions.explanation: A through ball helps a teammate run behind the defense to score.

questions.question: A compact defense blocks the direct route to goal. What can create an opening?
options: Move the ball and change supporting angles to draw defenders out
Keep forcing passes through the same blocked lane
Have everyone wait near the penalty spot
Dribble toward the largest group of defenders
questions.explanation: Use width, combinations, or a switch to move the defense. A patient backward pass may help create the next opening.

questions.question: If you're near the goal with the ball, what do you do?
options: Reset to midfield even if space is open
Shoot high from any angle
Look to shoot or pass quickly
Hold the ball until all defenders recover
questions.explanation: Check the keeper, defenders, and teammates before the ball arrives. When a useful chance appears, a quick controlled shot or pass can use it before the space closes.

questions.question: Your teammate starts a run behind the defense and the passing lane is open. What helps the pass connect?
options: Lead the run with the right timing and pace
Pass to where the runner started
Wait until a defender closes the lane
Use maximum power regardless of distance
questions.explanation: Time the pass and judge the runner's speed. Where offside applies, check their position when the ball is played.

questions.question: What is the benefit of switching the play?
options: It confuses teammates
It finds space on the other side
It makes it harder to pass
It delays the attack
questions.explanation: Switching helps attack open areas when one side is crowded.

questions.question: What helps attackers most when playing as a team?
options: Individual tricks only
Spacing, timing, and support
All players standing on the same line
Forward runs with no passing angle
questions.explanation: Attacking as a group needs movement and smart choices.

questions.question: You are unmarked near goal and a clear passing lane connects you to the ball. What is useful?
options: Be ready for a pass and a quick finish
Move behind the nearest defender
Stay facing away from the ball
Run toward the passer and close the space
questions.explanation: Being available includes a clear lane and being ready to receive. Unmarked does not always mean a pass can reach you.

questions.question: When attacking, where is the most dangerous space to go?
options: The middle in front of the goal
The sideline near halfway
The defensive third
The space behind your own back line
questions.explanation: The middle near the goal is the best area to create chances.

questions.question: You are outnumbered, the forward route is blocked, and support is arriving. What can help?
options: Protect or recycle the ball until support can join
Attack the largest group of defenders immediately
Force a pass through a blocked lane
Stop looking for teammates
questions.explanation: Holding the ball can buy time. Use a safe supporting pass if that is better than shielding. Attack quickly if a real opening appears.

questions.question: You win the ball and see open space before opponents recover. Why might you attack quickly?
options: Their defensive shape has not recovered yet
Every turnover requires a first-time forward pass
Your teammates can stop providing cover
The offside rule stops applying
questions.explanation: A quick attack can use the space before it closes. If no useful route is open, keeping the ball is a good choice.

questions.question: What is a cutback pass?
options: A pass from near the endline back toward open space
A pass into your own net
A throw-in
A pass only to the goalkeeper
questions.explanation: Cutbacks are dangerous because defenders often run toward goal and leave space behind them.

questions.question: What should the player without the ball do during a 2v1?
options: Stay wide enough to be a real passing option
Run right beside the ball carrier
Stand in the defender's cover shadow
Move behind the ball carrier only
questions.explanation: Good spacing makes the defender choose between stopping the dribble or the pass.

questions.question: What is a third-player run?
options: A run by a teammate who receives after two other players combine
A run that starts from an offside position
A defender holding the back line
A shot from midfield
questions.explanation: Third-player runs are hard to mark because the runner arrives from a different angle.

questions.question: When should an attacker hold the ball up?
options: When teammates need time to join the attack
Every time they get it
Only after the attack has already ended
When no teammate can support
questions.explanation: Holding the ball can turn a rushed attack into a stronger team attack.

questions.question: In a game using offside, why time a run behind the defense with the pass?
options: To be onside when a teammate plays the ball and arrive at the right moment
To be onside only when you receive the ball
To avoid ever running behind a defender
To wait until the passer has stopped moving
questions.explanation: Offside position is judged when a teammate plays or touches the ball, not when you receive it. Local youth formats may use different offside rules.

questions.question: A right-footed player starts on the left wing. What opportunity can that role create?
options: Moving inside onto their stronger foot to pass or shoot
Being required to stay on the touchline for the whole attack
Making their left foot unusable
Removing the need for a teammate to provide width
questions.explanation: This is a common inverted-winger role. Cutting inside can open passing or shooting angles, but the player should still read the defender and can go outside when it helps.

questions.question: An inverted winger moves inside and a full-back is free to overlap. What must the team balance?
options: Width on the outside and cover if the ball is lost
Getting every nearby player into the same inside lane
Keeping the full-back behind the ball in every attack
Sending both center-backs into the penalty area too
questions.explanation: The overlap can preserve width as the winger moves inside. Other players must adjust their support and protection against a counter-attack.

questions.question: Three defenders have shifted toward your left-side attack. Your right winger is open. What is the purpose of keeping the ball on the left briefly?
options: Draw pressure before switching when the route to the right is ready
Keep passing left even after every lane is blocked
Make the right winger move into the same crowd
Wait until the right winger is also marked
questions.explanation: An overload uses extra players in one area. It can draw defenders across and free the other side, but the switch still needs a safe route and good timing.

questions.question: A striker drops short and a center-back follows. What can another attacker look for?
options: A timed run into the space the center-back has left
The exact same short space beside the striker
A run straight beyond the line before the pass is possible
A position that blocks the striker's passing lane
questions.explanation: One player's movement can create a chance for another. Check the space, the passer, and the offside line before making the run.

questions.question: Your team has a 3v2 attack. One defender guards the passing lane while the other backs away from you. What should you read?
options: Whether carrying forward can make a defender commit before you release the ball
Which teammate you decided to pass to before the break
Only the distance to goal, ignoring both defenders
Only the farthest teammate, regardless of the passing lane
questions.explanation: Do not pass just because you have an extra player. Carrying into open space can make a defender choose, then the pass or shot may become clearer.
